name: King Oyster
summary: Thick-stem oyster. Cooler, slightly drier, and less fresh air than cluster oysters.
chamber_notes: High humidity plus lots of fresh air makes skinny kings. Keep humidity a bit lower once pins set.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). P. eryngii prefers cooler fruiting (often 12 to 18 °C) and modest air.

source_notes.title: Vendor cards
source_notes.detail: Published grow-card ranges from culinary spawn suppliers (FreshCap, North Spore, Out-Grow and similar). King oyster cards commonly list 80 to 85% humidity to thicken stems.

stages.name: Fruiting
stages.notes: Let stems elongate before caps flare if you want steak-cut kings.

light_recipe.why: Same dark spawn run as other oysters. Fruiting is blue-heavy because P. eryngii primordia respond to blue light. Hours and white percent are the oyster default (12 h, 20% / 92 lux). No king-oyster-specific lux was found.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 blue is roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum.

sources.title: Xie 2018 king oyster
sources.detail: Chunliang Xie et al., Comparative transcriptomics of Pleurotus eryngii reveals blue-light regulation of carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) at primordium differentiated into fruiting body stage, Genomics 110 (2018). Blue light induced primordium differentiation.

sources.title: Penn State oyster production
sources.detail: Daniel J. Royse, Cultivation of Oyster Mushrooms, Penn State College of Agricultural Sciences. First 12 to 21 days of spawn run may be completed without artificial lighting. After spawn run, 4 h of cool white fluorescent light at 50 to 300 lux may be provided. This recipe uses 12 h as a labeled default photoperiod, not a page-cited Stamets value, and maps 20% white to 92 lux, inside that 50 to 300 lux band.

sources.title: Stamets
sources.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms, Ten Speed Press. Used here as a general cultivation reference. This recipe does not take a photoperiod or lux number from a cited page in that book.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.
